title: Clemson Spineless okra
seoTitle: Clemson Spineless Okra: Variety Guide and Free Seeds
description: Clemson Spineless okra won an All-America Selections award in 1939 and still thrives in Texas heat. Its history, size, pods and how to get free seeds.
summary: Clemson Spineless is a classic okra with smooth, dark green pods and no prickly spines. It won an All-America Selections award in 1939, it's recommended for Texas gardens, and it's the variety Olivia's Garden Foundation grows and gives away.

items: Bred by the South Carolina Experiment Station
Smooth, dark green pods without spines
Recommended for Texas by Texas A&M AgriLife
First pods about 2 months after planting

blocks.text: Clemson Spineless was bred by the South Carolina Experiment Station and won a national [All-America Selections award in 1939](https://all-americaselections.org/product/okra-clemson-spineless/). More than 85 years later, Texas A&M AgriLife still recommends it for Texas gardens.

The name says what makes it special. Clemson Extension describes its pods as [dark green and without spines](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/), so they're easier to handle and pleasant to eat. Pick them young, around 2 to 4 inches, while they're tender.
Plants are tall and upright. Like most okra, they [flower about 2 months after planting](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/okra/), with pods ready to pick a few days later.

sections.title: Is Clemson Spineless good for Texas?

blocks.text: Yes. Texas A&M AgriLife lists Clemson Spineless among [the best okra varieties to grow in Texas](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/okra/). It loves heat and keeps producing through the summer when given full sun and regular water.

blocks.text: Clemson Spineless is open-pollinated, so seed you save grows into the same kind of plant next year. That's how Olivia's family has kept her plants going. See [how to save okra seeds](/okra/saving-okra-seeds) to keep your own line going.

faq.question: Why is it called Clemson Spineless?
faq.answer: It's named for its spineless pods, which are smooth to handle. It was bred by the South Carolina Experiment Station and won an All-America Selections award in 1939.

faq.question: How many days until Clemson Spineless okra is ready?
faq.answer: Plants usually flower about 2 months after planting, and the first pods are ready to pick a few days after that.

faq.question: Can I get free Clemson Spineless okra seeds?
faq.answer: Yes. Olivia's Garden Foundation mails a free packet of 10 Clemson Spineless seeds to anyone in the United States or Canada. [Request yours here](/okra/free-okra-seeds).
